title: Work Equipment & Hand Tools
whatItIs: Work equipment is anything used at work: hammers, knives, ladders, power tools, saws, dumpers. PUWER 1998 says it must be suitable, kept safe and used by trained people.

keyFacts.text: Employers MUST provide suitable equipment and only use it for jobs and conditions it suits.
Work equipment MUST be maintained in efficient working order and in good repair.
Everyone who uses work equipment MUST have had adequate training to use it safely.
You MUST NOT interfere with or misuse anything provided for health and safety, such as guards.

keyFacts: Never use a machine with a danger sign or tag on it. Only an authorised person may remove it.
Switch off and isolate or lock off before clearing blockages, cleaning or adjusting.

visual.caption: Protecting people from dangerous parts: the order PUWER reg 11 sets

items.title: Other guards
items.text: e.g. interlocks: the machine can't start until closed.

items.title: Jigs and holders
items.text: Or push-sticks, where guards can't fully protect.

items.title: Training
items.text: Instruction, training and supervision for any risk left.

Result recorded and kept until the next one

onTheTest.question: The guard on a power tool makes your job slower and more awkward. What should you do?
options: Take the guard off and put it back after
Keep the guard on and tell your supervisor
Tape the guard open so it can't get in the way
Use the tool without the guard if you're careful
onTheTest.why: INDG291: never remove safeguards, even if they make the job harder. HSW Act s8: don't misuse safety equipment.

onTheTest.question: Under PUWER, who must make sure that people who use work equipment have had adequate training?
onTheTest.why: PUWER reg 9: every employer shall ensure that all persons who use work equipment have received adequate training for health and safety.

traps: Hand tools like hammers and knives are work equipment too, not just machines.
Your own tools brought to work are still covered by PUWER.
Loose clothing, chains, rings or long hair can get caught in moving parts.
Don't distract anyone who is using a machine.
